a.text: I drafted the Minister's speech. Eleven pages. I quoted myself twice — as 'a promising young voice'.

choices.label: Who is the promising young voice?
Cut it to one page. Ministers read like toddlers.
choices.result: Anselm sulks, then produces a crisp single page. It is annoyingly good.

choices.label: Brilliant. Send it straight to Capital under your name.
choices.result: Capital receives eleven pages from a junior. Someone in HQ laughs out loud.

b.text: …A colleague. Anonymous. Very talented. Also, me.

choices.label: Keep one quote. Delete your name. Growth.
choices.result: Anselm accepts the edit like a man surrendering a kidney.

choices.label: I'll quote you at the reception. Promise.
choices.result: Anselm glows. He will remember this promise. Forever.

a.text: I've been invited to the yacht of a man who 'does imports'. Good for networking, right?

choices.label: Absolutely not. Ask Marcel what 'imports' means.
choices.result: Anselm stays ashore and looks the yacht up on Chercheur. He goes pale.

choices.label: Go, but take Ruth Vale as a witness.
choices.result: Ruth gets a scoop about canapés. Nothing illegal. Officially.

choices.label: Bring me a cocktail umbrella.
choices.result: You approved a yacht party. HQ will love the photos.

a.text: Someone has taken my stapler. The red one. It was issued in 1994.

choices.label: Have you asked Maxim?
I'll order you a new one. Today.
choices.result: A procurement form is born. It needs three signatures. Pavel is visibly touched.

choices.label: Pavel, the Minister lands in days.
choices.result: 'Ministers come and go,' says Pavel. 'The stapler was permanent.'

b.text: Maxim made a checklist about the stapler. The stapler is on it. Its location is not.

choices.label: Let's declare it a security incident. Formally.
choices.result: Pavel files the incident report with deep satisfaction. Morale soars in Administration.

choices.label: Let it go. Like the six ambassadors.
choices.result: Pavel stares at you for exactly as long as an ambassador's term.

a.text: Ambassador number three also wanted the VIP lounge 'sorted by Tuesday'. It was a Sunday.

choices.label: What did ambassador three do wrong?
choices.result: He believed the travel agent. Pavel shares a binder of lessons. Useful, if laminated.

choices.label: I'm not like the others.
choices.result: 'They all said that,' Pavel notes. He writes it in a small book.

choices.label: Help me, and you'll be the one in the memoirs.
choices.result: Pavel pretends not to care. He re-orders his binders by importance.

a.text: Three colleagues asked me to 'just translate quickly'. One was a novel. One was a menu. One was a love letter.

choices.label: Whose love letter?
From now on, translations go through me, in writing.
choices.result: The queue at Sola's desk shrinks to almost bearable.

choices.label: You're local staff. It's in your job description.
choices.result: Sola reads you the job description. It is two lines and neither mentions novels.

b.text: Professional secrecy. But it rhymes 'Bianca' with 'convoy'. Badly.

choices.label: I didn't hear that. Take the afternoon off.
choices.result: Sola gets an afternoon. The embassy gets a little gossip. Everyone wins.

choices.label: Translate it beautifully. For morale.
choices.result: Sola does a wonderful job. Somewhere, a convoy is very confused.

a.text: My cousin works in the Protocol Office. He could fast-track the landing permit. He wants a visa for his band.

choices.label: No favours. We do it by the book.
choices.result: Sola nods with genuine respect. The permit will take the scenic route.

choices.label: What kind of band?
choices.result: 'Ska-fusion with nose flute.' You ask Ines to look at the application. Gently.

choices.label: Done. Give him two visas.
choices.result: The permit lands overnight. So does an audit question from Capital.

a.text: I need the Minister to stand next to a well. Not to pose. To understand.

choices.label: What is there to understand about a well?
Fine, but one photo. Lucien will choose the angle.
choices.result: Elise agrees through her teeth. Lucien already has a mood board.

choices.label: The Minister is allergic to dust and nuance.
choices.result: Elise drafts a strongly-worded memo to herself.

b.text: That the pump was donated in 2009, broke in 2010, and has been photographed 47 times since.

choices.label: Then we repair it before the visit. Quietly.
choices.result: A real repair. No banner. Elise almost cries. Your budget almost cries too.

choices.label: Then he'll be photograph 48. With a sad face.
choices.result: Elise laughs despite herself. Then she stops laughing.

a.text: Sola won't speak to me since the 'cultural sensitivity workshop'. In my defence, I organised it for her.

choices.label: Did you ask her before you organised it?
choices.result: Silence. Elise goes to apologise. It goes better than expected.

choices.label: I'll mediate over lunch at Auntie's.
choices.result: Two people who like local food finally share one. Tense, but delicious.

choices.label: Stay out of her way until the visit.
choices.result: The feud is frozen, not solved. Like the embassy freezer.

a.text: Convoy plan. Seven cars. Two decoys. One goat, for local credibility.

choices.label: Why a goat?
No goat. No decoys. Three cars.
choices.result: Bianca salutes with the enthusiasm of a demoted general.

choices.label: Approved. All of it.
choices.result: Seven cars are ordered. The goat is negotiating its own fee.

b.text: Rural roadblocks wave through anything with a goat. Field-tested in 2011. Do not ask about 2012.

choices.label: Keep the goat. Lose the decoys.
choices.result: A sensible compromise. The goat is named 'Attaché'.

choices.label: What happened in 2012?
choices.result: 'Classified,' says Bianca. Her eye twitches. You drop it.

a.text: Lucien sent me a 'visually optimised' convoy spreadsheet. It has a sunset gradient.

choices.label: Tell him I love it. Then use yours.
choices.result: Diplomacy at its finest. Both of them think they won.

choices.label: Work together. Bring the gradient AND the logistics.
choices.result: Bianca and Lucien produce the first armoured pastel convoy plan in history.

choices.label: I'll ban gradients embassy-wide.
choices.result: Bianca has never respected you more. Lucien files a grievance.

a.text: There is a man in the visa queue who claims to be the Minister's cousin. He has a photo. It's a painting.

choices.label: A painting of what?
Fast-track him. Just in case.
choices.result: He was not the cousin. He was very grateful though. He tells everyone.

choices.label: Same queue as everyone. Like democracy.
choices.result: Ines quietly updates your file to 'possibly decent'.

b.text: The Minister, on a horse, fighting a dragon. Signed 'with love, cousin'.

choices.label: Hang it in the lobby. Morale.
choices.result: The dragon painting becomes the embassy mascot. Ines denies involvement.

choices.label: Refer him to the art attaché. We have none.
choices.result: He leaves to find one. The queue moves one place. Celebrations.

a.text: Four hundred people in the queue and Capital wants me at the airport to 'wave'.

choices.label: You stay. I'll wave double.
choices.result: Ines looks at you like you rescued a kitten from a printer.

choices.label: Waving is diplomacy, Ines.
choices.result: Ines waves at you. It is not friendly waving.

choices.label: Send Maxim to wave. He loves it.
choices.result: Maxim waves with such joy it makes the evening news.

a.text: Hashtag for the visit: #BellaLuxeMoment. Or #MinisterialVibes. Legal hates both.

choices.label: What does legal like?
No hashtags. We are a state, not a smoothie.
choices.result: Lucien mourns. The legal department sends you flowers.

choices.label: #MinisterialVibes. Go.
choices.result: It trends in Ombrazia. Mostly as a joke. Still counts.

b.text: '#OfficialStatementPending'. It has eleven followers. Ten are lawyers.

choices.label: Compromise: #BellaluxeListens.
choices.result: Even Ruth Vale admits it's decent. Ruth never admits anything.

choices.label: Let the parrot pick one.
choices.result: The parrot picks a word we cannot print. Lucien loves it anyway.

a.text: The Deputy Foreign Minister wants a selfie with the cat. I need your approval. And the cat's.

choices.label: The cat is not available for press.
choices.result: The cat agrees with you. It always does.

choices.label: Approved. Brush the cat first.
choices.result: The selfie goes viral. Minister Bako is delighted. The cat is unimpressed.

choices.label: Only if the cat gets a diplomatic passport.
choices.result: Ines refuses. The cat does not care. Morale skyrockets anyway.

a.text: I made a checklist of the checklists. Then I lost it. Should I make a checklist to find it?

choices.label: What is on the master checklist?
Maxim, breathe. Pick the three that matter.
choices.result: Maxim picks three. One is 'lunch'. Fair enough.

choices.label: Yes. Laminate it.
choices.result: Maxim laminates everything, including Pavel's sandwich.

b.text: 1. Find checklist. 2. Do checklist. 3. Celebrate. 4. Ask Pavel why he is sighing.

choices.label: Add: 5. Book the VIP lounge.
choices.result: Maxim calls the airport immediately. Inexplicably, it works.

choices.label: Perfect. Don't change a thing.
choices.result: Maxim beams. Pavel sighs in a slightly higher key.

a.text: Do you think I'll be an ambassador one day? I already practise waving.

choices.label: If you survive this week, you can survive anything.
choices.result: Maxim writes this on a post-it and sticks it to his forehead.

choices.label: Show me your wave.
choices.result: It is a magnificent wave. Ministerial, even.

choices.label: Ambassadors don't ask. They assume.
choices.result: Maxim begins assuming. Things get weird by lunchtime.

a.text: The Minister's office sent dietary requirements: 'no garlic, no gluten, no foreign words on the menu'.

choices.label: No foreign words?
Cook what you like. I'll handle the office.
choices.result: Ketu nods slowly. Somewhere, garlic is being prepared defiantly.

choices.label: Follow the list exactly.
choices.result: The menu says 'Food (hot)'. Ketu has quietly died inside.

b.text: So 'bouillabaisse' is out. I suggested 'fish soup with ambition'.

choices.label: Perfect. Print it in gold.
choices.result: The menu becomes a collector's item. Capital asks for a copy.

choices.label: Call it 'Soup diplomatique'.
choices.result: Ketu points out that is a foreign word. You lose an argument to a chef.

a.text: EU coffee morning: you ate exactly 17.6% of the cookies again. Celeste asked me for your recipe for shamelessness.

choices.label: It's not shameless, it's budget proportional.
choices.result: Ketu bakes a cookie shaped like a pie chart. It's 17.6% chocolate.

choices.label: Bake for the next meeting. Win them over.
choices.result: Ketu's cookies end the cookie war. For now.

choices.label: Make them slightly worse. Strategic.
choices.result: Ketu refuses on artistic grounds. You respect that. Kind of.

a.text: Your landing permit has two stamps and a coffee ring. The coffee ring is not an official stamp. Yet.

choices.label: What would make it official?
I'll redo the form tonight. Personally.
choices.result: Ndao inclines his head by exactly two degrees. A historic thaw.

choices.label: Surely the Minister's plane can land anyway?
choices.result: 'Planes can land,' says Ndao. 'Whether they can leave is another form.'

b.text: A committee. Meeting quarterly. Next quarter.

choices.label: Then let's honour the coffee as tradition.
choices.result: Ndao almost smiles. Almost. The coffee ring is accepted 'exceptionally'.

choices.label: Could a gift basket speed things up?
choices.result: Ndao looks at you like you suggested a duel. Points lost.

a.text: Seating plan for the dinner. Your Minister is next to the Minister of Fisheries. Is that acceptable?

choices.label: Is Fisheries an important ministry?
choices.result: 'In a port city?' says Ndao. You have learned something.

choices.label: We demand the President's left hand.
choices.result: Ndao notes your demand. The President's left hand is apparently already 'politically spoken for'.

choices.label: Perfectly acceptable. Delightful even.
choices.result: Ndao records your flexibility. Future favours become slightly more possible.

a.text: Before you say it: yes, 17.6%. We counted. Please do not bring a calculator again.

choices.label: I would never bring a calculator.
I'll skip the cookies today. As a gesture.
choices.result: The room stares. Someone checks if you are ill. EU relations improve.

choices.label: 17.6%, Celeste. It's in the treaties.
choices.result: Pained expressions all round. A Nordic colleague sighs in three languages.

b.text: You brought an abacus. That is worse.

choices.label: It's a vintage abacus. Cultural heritage.
choices.result: Celeste laughs for the first time this year. Minutes record 'levity'.

choices.label: Fine. I'll take 17%. Rounded down, for unity.
choices.result: A historic compromise. Someone proposes a press release.

a.text: We need a joint EU statement on the volcano. Twenty-seven drafts. One volcano.

choices.label: Use the word 'concerned'. Everyone loves 'concerned'.
choices.result: Twenty-six nod. One wants 'deeply concerned'. Progress.

choices.label: Let Bellaluxe draft. We have a lighthouse.
choices.result: Celeste is unsure how lighthouses relate. She lets you try.

choices.label: Skip it. The volcano won't read it.
choices.result: Technically true. Diplomatically catastrophic.

a.text: The VIP lounge? Fully booked. For you, a 'cancellation' could occur. Unprompted. Mostly.

choices.label: What does 'mostly' cost?
No thank you. We'll wait for a real cancellation.
choices.result: Marcel shrugs. 'Real' is such an old-fashioned word.

choices.label: Make it happen.
choices.result: A cancellation happens. A sports team is stranded in Lounge B. They chirp about it.

b.text: A dinner. With a man. Who would like a photo. With your flag.

choices.label: Only if it's a very small flag.
choices.result: Marcel admires your style. A tiny flag is procured.

choices.label: No photos. I'll pay the dinner.
choices.result: Marcel chooses the Gilded Palm. Your budget weeps into a gold napkin.

a.text: Rumour says your Minister snores in meetings. I could… adjust that rumour.

choices.label: Adjust it how?
choices.result: He suggests 'meditates actively'. Lucien wants to trademark it.

choices.label: Leave rumours alone.
choices.result: Marcel looks disappointed in you. Like a dad at a school play.

choices.label: Start a better rumour about Ombrazia's minister.
choices.result: A rumour spreads. It spreads back. Host goodwill dips.

a.text: Off the record: is it true your embassy owns a parrot that knows the server password?

choices.label: Is that a real question?
No comment. On the record.
choices.result: Ruth writes 'no comment' and underlines it twice. Never good.

choices.label: Off the record: yes. And it's 'Cracker123'.
choices.result: Ruth laughs and promises not to print it. You change the password anyway.

b.text: Ruth: 'Everything is a real question in this bar.'

choices.label: Then the real answer is: ask the cat.
choices.result: The cat ignores Ruth. Ruth respects the cat. You gain a friend.

choices.label: I'll trade you a better story.
choices.result: You hint at the 17.6% cookie scandal. Ruth is delighted.

a.text: You're buying, right? Correspondents' rules: the diplomat pays, the journalist remembers.

choices.label: Of course. Something local.
choices.result: Ruth approves of your choice. She'll remember it fondly. Mostly.

choices.label: Let's split. Like an EU budget.
choices.result: Ruth calculates 17.6% of the bill. She has heard of you.

choices.label: Diplomats never pay. We submit claims.
choices.result: Ruth writes that down. It will be paragraph three.

a.text: My caddie says your Minister needs a meeting. My caddie also says I'm a scratch golfer. Both are lies.

choices.label: How bad is your handicap, Minister?
Let me carry your bag. Diplomatically.
choices.result: Bako hands you the bag. It weighs as much as a protocol file.

choices.label: Thirty minutes, Minister. Tuesday?
choices.result: Bako chuckles. 'Nobody has Tuesday. Have a Thursday.'

b.text: 'Handicap is a colonial concept,' says Bako. 'I count only good shots.'

choices.label: Then you're unbeaten. Like our friendship.
choices.result: Bako roars with laughter and agrees to a working breakfast.

choices.label: Thirty-six, then.
choices.result: Accurate. Painfully. Bako forgets your name for the next nine holes.

a.text: A friendly bet: if I sink this putt, your Minister visits my constituency. If I miss, you buy dinner.

choices.label: Deal.
choices.result: He sinks it. Somehow the green tilted. The Minister's programme gains a fish market.

choices.label: I'd rather lose on purpose.
choices.result: Bako is insulted you'd fake it. And delighted you'd try.

choices.label: I don't gamble with programmes.
choices.result: Bako calls you 'refreshingly boring'. It is not a compliment.

a.text: Six agencies. One programme. Each wants its logo bigger than the others.

choices.label: How big are we talking?
Put them in a circle. Nobody's on top.
choices.result: The logos form a circle. It looks like a pizza. Everyone is equally unhappy. Success.

choices.label: Bellaluxe's logo goes in the middle. We pay.
choices.result: Dr Chen notes your generosity and your ego in the same memo.

b.text: One agency's logo is now larger than the project itself.

choices.label: Then let's build a bigger project.
choices.result: Dr Chen laughs. Then writes it down. Then thinks about it seriously.

choices.label: Make the logos fridge magnets.
choices.result: The fridge magnets are a hit. The programme still needs funding.

a.text: Your Minister's office asked what 'UNDAF-PPCC-WGSD' stands for. Honestly, so do I.

choices.label: Let's make up a new acronym. Shorter.
choices.result: You invent 'HELP'. Three agencies already claim it.

choices.label: Translate it into normal words for him.
choices.result: 'Some people meeting about other meetings.' Dr Chen approves.

choices.label: Tell him it's classified.
choices.result: It is not. Dr Chen is unimpressed.

a.text: Valdoria's national anthem has seven verses. Protocol insists the reception cannot begin until the choir has found the last one.

choices.label: Offer the choir a discreet glass of water.
choices.result: Mara thanks you. The choir finds verse seven, and the water.

choices.label: Suggest starting the reception at verse four.
choices.result: Mara calls it a bold proposal for constitutional reform.

a.text: My seating plan has a reserved chair for every ambassador and one for the person who actually knows where the venue is.

choices.label: Make sure the driver gets the good chair.
choices.result: Mara moves the driver closer to the door, which everyone agrees is wise.

choices.label: Ask for the chair closest to the camera.
choices.result: Mara offers you the camera's carrying case instead.

a.text: Asteria has agreed to the EU27 consensus, subject to a footnote longer than the consensus.

choices.label: Help shorten the footnote together.
choices.result: Niko removes two semicolons and calls the result historic.

choices.label: Propose a footnote to the footnote.
choices.result: Niko reaches for a second page. Nobody gets lunch.

a.text: At the last EU27 meeting, Niko counted the coffee cups to establish whether everyone had been consulted.

choices.label: Offer to bring an extra pot next time.
choices.result: Niko records your offer under practical cooperation.

choices.label: Demand an audit of the teaspoons.
choices.result: Niko opens a spreadsheet and the room falls silent.
